proposed_fix.description: Confirm packet loss/network errors on the node hosting checkoutservice, then gated reschedule of the checkoutservice pod to a different node if confirmed.
steps: Identify the node and pod(s) running checkoutservice (kubectl get pod -o wide) and check node network receive/transmit error and drop counters (e.g. node_network_receive_errs_total, node_network_transmit_drop_total) for that node.
Check conntrack usage on that node (node_nf_conntrack_entries vs limit) to rule out table exhaustion as the source of drops, given the socket increase in E4.
Check for other pods on the same node generating heavy network traffic and whether node CPU/memory headroom is left for networking.

If the node shows errors or drops, after human approval cordon the node and delete one checkoutservice pod so it reschedules onto a healthy node; watch checkoutservice latency-50/90 and frontend_error for recovery.

If conntrack is near its limit, after approval consider migrating noisy pods off the node first; only raise the conntrack limit as a last resort, as a non-persistent change that is reviewed before being made persistent.
If no node-level network errors are found, escalate to inspect the pod's network path (CNI, pod-to-pod links) rather than making changes.
preconditions: Confirm the node hosting checkoutservice shows network errors/drops or conntrack pressure; otherwise do not move pods.
Confirm other healthy nodes have spare CPU/memory capacity for checkoutservice.
Confirm checkoutservice has more than one replica or that a brief restart is acceptable, since frontend errors are already elevated (E1).
Human approval obtained before any cordon, delete, or limit change.
proposed_fix.rollback: Uncordon the node (kubectl uncordon) and, if needed, scale or reschedule checkoutservice back; revert any conntrack sysctl change to its previous value.
